prize_parts.citation: for the development of dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electrons

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged. B026 remains the strongest case for a physical framework that made an important class of quantum materials quantitatively intelligible. DMFT connected local many-body physics with metal-insulator behavior, spectral properties, and magnetism in correlated solids, and it has endured through extensive comparison with electronic-structure work and spectroscopy. Georges, Kotliar, and Vollhardt are a defensible representation of the foundational large-dimensional route and the formulation that made DMFT a broadly usable theory. The citation should reward that conceptual development, not the later ecosystem of solvers and materials applications.
statement.case_against: The attribution boundary remains the decisive reservation. DMFT developed through antecedent work, foundational limiting constructions, impurity-solver advances, and material-specific implementations, so a historical review must establish that the proposed trio captures the decisive theoretical development without claiming the whole subsequent enterprise. This is a real weakness relative to achievements with more sharply bounded individual credit.

responses.point: Mehlig argues that B048 unites a clear universality-class discovery with unusually direct quantitative experimental confirmation, whereas DMFT credit is distributed among foundations, formulation, solvers, and implementations.
responses.response: I agree that B048 has an admirable theory-to-experiment arc and that its credit boundary deserves serious respect. I retain B026 because DMFT supplied a general working description for correlations in real electronic materials, not simply a successful model class. The appropriate limitation is to recognize the foundational theory narrowly; later solver and implementation work should not be folded into the citation.

responses.point: Olsson argues that B055 overcame a fundamental electron-optical limitation and transformed microscopy into a reproducible atomic-scale quantitative capability, while identifying unresolved priority among correction approaches and implementation teams.
responses.response: I share Olsson's high assessment of B055 and retain it as my leading experimental alternative. It has exceptional maturity and has transformed how materials can be observed. The unresolved division among theory, competing correction concepts, prototypes, and practical realization is nevertheless substantial. B026 has a similarly important attribution task, but its central theoretical formulation can be delimited more directly if the citation remains confined to DMFT itself.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that B020 identifies a coherent recollision mechanism and quantum theory, extensively validated and foundational for high-harmonic and attosecond science, provided it is separated from the wider experimental revolution.
responses.response: I accept this delimitation and regard B020 as a very strong alternative. Its mechanism-to-experiment maturity is persuasive. DMFT remains ahead for me because it has reorganized the description of correlated electrons across many material classes and sustained demanding quantitative confrontation with measured spectra; nevertheless, B020 has the advantage that its proposed theoretical subject can be stated with unusual clarity.

uncertainties: Whether historical review confirms that Georges, Kotliar, and Vollhardt are the most defensible three-person allocation for the foundational development of DMFT.
How narrowly the citation must distinguish the large-dimensional foundation and modern DMFT formulation from impurity solvers and later material-specific implementations.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
